nodes.label: The Skin: Structure, Biochemistry, and Function
nodes.summary: Comprehensive overview of skin morphology, the epidermal keratinizing system, terminal differentiation, pigmentation, dermis, appendages, hair and nails. It covers barrier function and penetration pathways of cosmetic actives, immunology, cytokines, enzymes, UV-induced photodamage and skin cancer, and gene expression (genomics) in skin care.

nodes.label: Skin
nodes.summary: Organ forming the border between organism and environment; prevents dehydration, blocks noxious materials and microbes, cushions shock, regulates temperature. Divided into epidermis, dermis and subcutaneous tissue.

nodes.label: Epidermis
nodes.summary: Outermost skin layer, a stratified squamous epithelium 0.05-1.5 mm thick (about 100 micrometers typical), made primarily of keratinocytes; replaced about every 42 days.

nodes.label: Dermis
nodes.summary: Layer beneath the epidermis (0.3-3.0 mm) of protein fibers in a GAG-rich ground substance; divided into papillary and reticular layers; cushions against mechanical injury and nourishes the epidermis.

nodes.label: Hypodermis
nodes.summary: Deepest skin layer (subcutis), composed primarily of lipocytes with fibrous septae for structure and support.

nodes.label: Keratinocyte
nodes.summary: Main epidermal cell type (about 95% of epidermis) producing keratin and cytokines; matures outward from the basal layer to become corneocytes.

nodes.label: Keratin
nodes.summary: Family of fibrous structural proteins formed from intermediate filaments; type I acidic (K9-K20) and type II basic (K1-K8) keratins pair as dimers; key component of stratum corneum, hair and nails.

nodes.label: Stratum Basale
nodes.summary: Innermost epidermal layer of cuboidal/columnar proliferating cells attached to the basement membrane by hemidesmosomes; houses epidermal stem cells; biomarkers keratins K5 and K14.

nodes.label: Stratum Spinosum
nodes.summary: Prickle layer named for numerous desmosomes; lamellar granules appear in its upper region; biomarkers keratins K1 and K10.

nodes.label: Stratum Granulosum
nodes.summary: Granular layer containing keratohyalin granules and abundant lamellar bodies (about 20% of cell volume in uppermost cells); 1 to 10 cell layers thick.

nodes.label: Stratum Lucidum
nodes.summary: Clear layer at the deepest portion of the stratum corneum, recognizable only in palmar and plantar skin.

nodes.label: Stratum Corneum
nodes.summary: Outermost horny layer of 10-15 layers of anucleate corneocytes in an intercellular lipid matrix (about 10 micrometers); replaced in about 14 days; constitutes 10% of skin but over 80% of barrier function.

nodes.label: Dermal-Epidermal Junction
nodes.summary: Basement membrane zone between epidermis and dermis composed of basal cell plasma membrane, lamina lucida, basal lamina and dermal fibrils.

nodes.label: Melanocyte
nodes.summary: Neural crest-derived dendritic cell in the basal layer that produces melanosomes; each serves about 36-40 keratinocytes (epidermal melanin unit); number is the same regardless of skin color.

nodes.label: Langerhans Cell
nodes.summary: Epidermal resident dendritic antigen-presenting cell (3-5% of suprabasal cells) with Birbeck granules; captures antigens via langerin; impaired by UVB and decreases with age.

nodes.label: Merkel Cell
nodes.summary: Epidermal cell of the basal layer concerned with sensation, often associated with sensory nerve endings.

nodes.label: Dendritic Cell
nodes.summary: Antigen-presenting immune cells; at least four dermal subclasses that capture and present antigens to T-lymphocytes and induce tolerance.

nodes.label: Desmosome
nodes.summary: Intercellular bridge connecting keratinocytes; gives the stratum spinosum its spiny appearance; corneodesmosomes connect corneocytes (desmocollin, desmoglein).

nodes.label: Lamellar Body
nodes.summary: Golgi-derived secretory organelle (0.1-0.5 micrometers) appearing in the stratum spinosum; secretes lipids, hydrolytic enzymes and antimicrobial peptides at the SG-SC interface; about 985 proteins identified.

nodes.label: Keratohyalin Granule
nodes.summary: Basophilic granules of the stratum granulosum composed of profilaggrin, loricrin and keratins; responsible for keratin filament aggregation; absent in hard keratins of hair and nail.

nodes.label: Filaggrin
nodes.summary: Histidine-rich filament-aggregating protein from keratohyalin (from profilaggrin) that aligns keratin into macrofibers; then hydrolyzed into free amino acids of NMF; mutations linked to atopic dermatitis and ichthyosis vulgaris.

nodes.label: Profilaggrin
nodes.summary: High molecular weight, histidine-rich, highly phosphorylated precursor protein dephosphorylated and clipped into filaggrin units.

nodes.label: Natural Moisturizing Factor
nodes.summary: Water-soluble hygroscopic compounds, mainly free amino acids from filaggrin breakdown, representing about 10% of corneocyte mass, that hold water in the stratum corneum.

nodes.label: Corneocyte
nodes.summary: Terminally differentiated, anucleate, keratin-filled keratinocyte forming the bricks of the stratum corneum; enclosed by a cross-linked cornified envelope.

nodes.label: Involucrin
nodes.summary: Primary cytoplasmic precursor protein of the cornified cell envelope, cross-linked with loricrin by transglutaminase.

nodes.label: Loricrin
nodes.summary: Cross-linked protein of the cornified envelope found in keratohyalin granules.

nodes.label: Transglutaminase
nodes.summary: Calcium-dependent enzyme catalyzing epsilon-(gamma-glutamyl) lysine crosslinks of involucrin and loricrin to form the cornified envelope.

nodes.label: Cornified Envelope
nodes.summary: Rigid, chemically resistant cross-linked protein band with covalently bound omega-hydroxyceramide lipid layer replacing the corneocyte plasma membrane.

nodes.label: Ceramide
nodes.summary: Major stratum corneum intercellular lipid class; generated from glucosylceramides; covalently bound to corneocyte envelopes; requires very-long-chain fatty acids (ELOVL4).

nodes.label: Cholesterol
nodes.summary: Stratum corneum barrier lipid secreted via lamellar bodies; rate-limiting enzyme of its synthesis is HMG-CoA reductase.

nodes.label: Free Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Stratum corneum lipid component together with ceramides and cholesterol; synthesis rate-limited by acetyl-CoA carboxylase.

nodes.label: Glucosylceramide
nodes.summary: Lamellar granule lipid converted by beta-glucocerebrosidase into stratum corneum ceramides.

nodes.label: Cholesterol Sulfate
nodes.summary: Minor SC lipid that inhibits serine proteases, protecting corneodesmosomes until degraded by sterol sulfatase in outer layers.

nodes.label: Kallikrein
nodes.summary: Serine proteases co-localized to lamellar bodies that progressively dissolve corneodesmosomes for orderly desquamation.

nodes.label: Antimicrobial Peptide
nodes.summary: Peptides such as beta-defensins (hBD-2) and cathelicidins packaged in lamellar bodies, linking permeability and antimicrobial barriers.

nodes.label: Tight Junction
nodes.summary: Cell junctions crucial for the epidermal permeability barrier; Langerhans cells extend dendrites through them.

nodes.label: Melanin
nodes.summary: Pigment derived from tyrosine formed in melanosomes; major determinant of skin color; a stable free radical; barrier to UV radiation.

nodes.label: Eumelanin
nodes.summary: Brown to black melanin formed via indole-5,6-quinone; a poikilopolymer; seen in dark hair.

nodes.label: Pheomelanin
nodes.summary: Yellow to red melanin formed from DOPA-quinone and cysteine via cysteinyldopa; predominates in blond hair.

nodes.label: Melanosome
nodes.summary: Melanocyte organelle in which tyrosinase forms melanin; number and size, not melanocyte count, determine skin color.

nodes.label: Tyrosinase
nodes.summary: Enzyme in melanosomes catalyzing melanin formation by oxidation of tyrosine to DOPA and DOPAquinone.

nodes.label: Tyrosine
nodes.summary: Amino acid precursor of melanin, oxidized to DOPA.

nodes.label: Melanogenesis
nodes.summary: Formation of melanin: tyrosine oxidized to DOPA, dehydrogenated to DOPAquinone, then eumelanin via indole-5,6-quinone or pheomelanin via cysteinyldopa; depends on free radical generation.

nodes.label: Collagen
nodes.summary: Major dermal fiber (75% of dry weight, 18-30% of volume) rich in glycine, hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine; made by fibroblasts from procollagen; vitamin C and copper are cofactors.

nodes.label: Elastin
nodes.summary: Elastic fiber protein, 4% of dermal dry weight, containing the unique amino acid desmosine; provides resilience.

nodes.label: Reticulin
nodes.summary: Fine silver-staining dermal fibers (0.4% of dry weight), now regarded as type III collagen, anchoring the basal lamina.

nodes.label: Glycosaminoglycan
nodes.summary: Acidic polysaccharides of the dermal ground substance (hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate, dermatan sulfate) holding copious water.

nodes.label: Hyaluronic Acid
nodes.summary: Major glycosaminoglycan of the dermal ground substance; very high molecular weight and water-binding.

nodes.label: Fibroblast
nodes.summary: Mesenchyme-derived principal dermal cell that secretes collagen, procollagen and other matrix constituents.

nodes.label: Mast Cell
nodes.summary: Mesenchymal dermal cell with heparin and histamine granules; active participant in inflammation and irritation.

nodes.label: Eccrine Sweat Gland
nodes.summary: Most numerous skin appendage (up to 600/cm2), cholinergically controlled, producing odorless dilute sweat (Cl-, Na+, lactic acid, urea) for thermoregulation.

nodes.label: Apocrine Gland
nodes.summary: Tubular gland attached to hair follicles in axillae, anogenital region; adrenergically controlled; odor arises from bacterial action on secretions.

nodes.label: Sebaceous Gland
nodes.summary: Holocrine gland, usually attached to hair follicles, densest on scalp, face, chest (400-900/cm2); androgen-stimulated; cell division to rupture takes about 14 days.

nodes.label: Sebum
nodes.summary: Sebaceous lipid: triglycerides 57.5%, wax esters 26%, squalene 12%, free fatty acids 10%, minor cholesterol; thermoregulatory, antimicrobial; excess associated with acne.

nodes.label: Androgen
nodes.summary: Male sex hormones (e.g., testosterone) of gonadal and adrenal origin that stimulate sebaceous gland activity.

nodes.label: Estrogen
nodes.summary: Female sex hormone; inhibits sebaceous secretion in humans.

nodes.label: Cyproterone Acetate
nodes.summary: Anti-androgen that inhibits sebaceous secretion.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle
nodes.summary: Variable appendage producing terminal, vellus or lanugo hair; hair color from melanosomes of bulb melanocytes; accounts for 1-2% of skin surface and a penetration route.

nodes.label: Nail Plate
nodes.summary: Keratinized cells originating in the nail matrix, without keratohyalin granules; cuticle formed by proximal nail fold.

nodes.label: Terminal Differentiation
nodes.summary: Three-to-four-week conversion of basal keratinocytes into flat corneocytes involving keratin formation, lipid processing, water loss (80-85% to about 35%), and envelope cross-linking.

nodes.label: Desquamation
nodes.summary: Shedding of corneocytes from the skin surface, in equilibrium with basal mitosis; enabled by protease degradation of corneodesmosomes.

nodes.label: Transepidermal Water Loss
nodes.summary: Water diffusing/evaporating from the body through the epidermis; increased by barrier disruption (wounds, solvents, surfactants); a key measure in skin care development.

nodes.label: Skin Barrier Function
nodes.summary: Epidermal permeability barrier located in the stratum corneum, demonstrated by Blank and Scheuplein; interdependent with antimicrobial, immune, antioxidant and UV barriers.

nodes.label: Brick and Mortar Model
nodes.summary: Model of the stratum corneum with corneocytes as bricks and intercellular lipids as mortar; later extended to a composite smart material concept.

nodes.label: Intercellular Penetration Pathway
nodes.summary: Tortuous route between corneocytes through intercellular lipids (gaps about 0.013 micrometers); main route for most hydrophilic and lipophilic molecules.

nodes.label: Transcellular Penetration Pathway
nodes.summary: Penetration through corneocytes; route for amphiphilic and small molecules; slow but large surface area.

nodes.label: Follicular Penetration Pathway
nodes.summary: Trans-appendageal route through hair follicles (1-2% of skin surface) for large insoluble molecules and nanoparticles.

nodes.label: Polar Penetration Pathway
nodes.summary: Hydrophilic route through polar pores surrounded by polar lipids between cells; e.g., sucrose penetrates this way.

nodes.label: Skin Penetration
nodes.summary: Passive diffusion of actives through the stratum corneum; only molecules under 500 Da penetrate; depends on skin condition, site, hydration, molecular size and vehicle.

nodes.label: Liposome
nodes.summary: Phospholipid/cholesterol bilayer vesicle carrier for hydrophilic or lipophilic actives; five proposed mechanisms of SC penetration; conventional liposomes do not penetrate intact.

nodes.label: Transfersome
nodes.summary: Deformable liposome containing surfactant in its bilayer that can deform and pass intact between SC cells following the water gradient (Cevc).

nodes.label: Nanoparticle
nodes.summary: Nanosized carriers penetrating via intercellular and follicular pathways; can deliver lipophilic compounds without transdermal penetration with up to 5000-fold solubilization; used in sunscreens and foundations.

nodes.label: Intelligent Targeting Carrier
nodes.summary: PLGA capsules with PVA shell and covalently bound peptide ligands recognized by fibroblasts, melanocytes or adipocytes to deliver actives intracellularly.

nodes.label: Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)
nodes.summary: Polymer matrix of targeted capsules delivering actives to cells such as dendritic cells.

nodes.label: Polyvinyl Alcohol
nodes.summary: Polymer forming the outer shell of PLGA intelligent targeting capsules.

nodes.label: Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Molecules that help the stratum corneum regenerate and protect itself and underlying layers from UV and environmental toxins.

nodes.label: T-Lymphocyte
nodes.summary: Immune cells activated by antigen-presenting Langerhans/dendritic cells; Th1/Th2 clonal expansion yields allergen-specific sensitivity.

nodes.label: Langerin
nodes.summary: Calcium-dependent C-type lectin (CD207) binding mannose; antigen capture receptor on Langerhans cells that induces Birbeck granules.

nodes.label: Birbeck Granule
nodes.summary: Tennis-racquet-shaped rod organelle characteristic of Langerhans cells into which captured antigen is routed.

nodes.label: Contact Sensitization
nodes.summary: Allergen-mediated activation of Langerhans cells which migrate to lymph nodes (CCL19) and activate allergen-specific T-cells.

nodes.label: Cytokine
nodes.summary: Small signaling proteins/glycoproteins from keratinocytes, LCs, macrophages, fibroblasts, lymphocytes (interleukins, interferons, TNF, CSFs, growth factors); production rises upon challenge.

nodes.label: Toll-Like Receptor
nodes.summary: Membrane proteins binding pathogen components (bacterial DNA, LPS, flagellin, beta-glucan) that regulate cytokine production.

nodes.label: Acetyl-CoA Carboxylase
nodes.summary: Biotin-dependent rate-limiting enzyme of epidermal fatty acid synthesis, converting acetyl-CoA to malonyl-CoA.

nodes.label: HMG-CoA Reductase
nodes.summary: Rate-limiting enzyme of epidermal cholesterol biosynthesis using NADPH.

nodes.label: Serine Palmitoyl Transferase
nodes.summary: Rate-limiting enzyme in sphingolipid synthesis.

nodes.label: Beta-Glucocerebrosidase
nodes.summary: Lamellar body enzyme converting glucosylceramides to ceramides; critical to barrier competency.

nodes.label: Psoriasis
nodes.summary: Chronic immune/genetic inflammatory disease with abnormally rapid transformation of basal cells into horny cells, scaling plaques, T-cell and neutrophil infiltration; treated with anti-TNF, anti-IL-12/23.

nodes.label: Ichthyosis
nodes.summary: Family of genetic disorders of dry scaling skin; ichthyosis vulgaris results from abnormal retention of keratinocytes and filaggrin mutations.

nodes.label: Atopic Dermatitis
nodes.summary: Itchy chronic skin inflammation with barrier dysfunction; associated with filaggrin mutations and unique gene expression profiles.

nodes.label: Acne
nodes.summary: Skin disorder associated with excessive sebum production.

nodes.label: Rosacea
nodes.summary: Skin disorder with unique gene expression profile; main feature is facial redness.

nodes.label: UV Radiation
nodes.summary: Ultraviolet radiation causes photodamage, premature aging, immunosuppression, DNA mutations and skin cancer; a complete carcinogen (initiator and promoter).

nodes.label: UVB Radiation
nodes.summary: UV band harming mainly the epidermis via direct DNA absorption forming pyrimidine dimers (signature mutations) and indirectly via ROS; impairs Langerhans cells.

nodes.label: UVA Radiation
nodes.summary: UV band penetrating to the dermis, damaging DNA indirectly via chromophore-generated ROS, activating metalloproteinases and decreasing immune recognition.

nodes.label: Pyrimidine Dimer
nodes.summary: DNA lesion formed between adjacent pyrimidines by direct UVB absorption, producing UVB signature mutations.

nodes.label: Reactive Oxygen Species
nodes.summary: Oxidants generated by UVB/UVA that indirectly damage DNA and drive photoaging.

nodes.label: Matrix Metalloproteinase
nodes.summary: Enzymes activated by UVA that break down collagen and elastic tissue, causing sagging and wrinkles.

nodes.label: Photoaging
nodes.summary: Premature skin aging from UV exposure: leathery thickened outer shell, mottled pigmentation, sagging and wrinkles.

nodes.label: Actinic Keratosis
nodes.summary: Premalignant hyperkeratotic lesion of photodamaged skin with p53/p16 mutations; may progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

nodes.label: Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer
nodes.summary: Most common cancer (about one million new US cases yearly), increasing with cumulative sun exposure; includes BCC and SCC.

nodes.label: Basal Cell Carcinoma
nodes.summary: Most common NMSC (about 75% of skin cancers); locally invasive, does not metastasize.

nodes.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
nodes.summary: About 20% of skin cancers; about 2% metastasize.

nodes.label: Melanoma
nodes.summary: Cutaneous malignant melanoma, about 5% of skin cancers; metastasizes with high mortality once invasive.

nodes.label: Skin Cancer
nodes.summary: Classified as nonmelanoma skin cancer and cutaneous malignant melanoma; one in five Americans will develop one; linked to sun exposure and tanning beds.

nodes.label: Sunscreen
nodes.summary: OTC products with UV-absorbing agents that help lower the incidence of skin cancer.

nodes.label: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
nodes.summary: Ubiquitous combustion pollutants (e.g., benzo[a]pyrene from exhaust and cigarette smoke) synergistic with UVA in oxidative damage.

nodes.label: Fitzpatrick Skin Type Classification
nodes.summary: Skin phototype scale (I-VI) based on tanning ability and sunburn propensity; NMSC highest in types I and II.

nodes.label: Apoptosis
nodes.summary: Programmed cell death that removes cells with excessive DNA damage.

nodes.label: Genomics
nodes.summary: Field of high-throughput gene analysis arising from the Human Genome Project (completed 2003, 3 billion base pairs); with other omics enables advances in dermatology and cosmetics.

nodes.label: Gene Expression Analysis
nodes.summary: Measurement of which genes are turned on/off (microarrays, qPCR) used in cosmetics to screen raw materials, show efficacy and mechanism, and assess safety.

nodes.label: Microarray
nodes.summary: Go-to high-throughput method for simultaneous analysis of thousands of genes to identify biomarkers; Taylor et al. found 1282 genes in differentiating keratinocytes.

nodes.label: Quantitative Real-Time PCR
nodes.summary: qPCR enables accurate quantification of gene expression and detection of mutations.

nodes.label: Next-Generation Sequencing
nodes.summary: State-of-the-art sequencing of whole genomes in days, RNA sequencing and epigenetic analysis.

nodes.label: Epigenetics
nodes.summary: Mechanisms such as DNA methylation that may elucidate aging, photoaging and skin disease; emerging in product development.

nodes.label: Personalized Skin Care
nodes.summary: Using an individual's genetic footprint to develop skin care products addressing specific needs.

nodes.label: MicroRNA
nodes.summary: Small RNAs regulating genes such as p63 in proliferating and differentiating keratinocytes.

nodes.label: CYP26B1
nodes.summary: Cytochrome P450 enzyme in epidermal keratinocytes essential for retinoic acid metabolism; ablation disrupts barrier formation.

nodes.label: Retinoic Acid
nodes.summary: Retinoid metabolized by CYP26b1 in keratinocytes; increased levels disrupt embryonic barrier formation.

nodes.label: Ascorbic Acid
nodes.summary: Vitamin C; cofactor required in collagen biosynthesis.

nodes.label: Copper
nodes.summary: Cofactor required in collagen biosynthesis.

nodes.label: In Vitro Skin Model
nodes.summary: Cell cultures and artificial skin used for screening; lack melanocytes, Langerhans cells and a realistic barrier.

nodes.label: Classification Scale for Skin Complexions Around the World
nodes.summary: Argues that the 1975 Fitzpatrick scale fails to predict skin type and precautions across races and proposes the EP Global Skin Classification Scale (classes I-XI) based on race, country of origin, complexion, skin characteristics, skin type and precautions. The scale derives from a 1997-2005 San Francisco clinic study of 588 subjects using skin evaluation questionnaires, Wood's lamp and UV photography.

nodes.label: EP Global Skin Classification Scale
nodes.summary: Eleven-class skin classification by Eva Patel (2012) covering race, country of origin, complexion, skin characteristics, skin type and precautions, designed to fill gaps of the Fitzpatrick scale.

nodes.label: EP Class I (Caucasian I)
nodes.summary: Northern European/Canadian origin; pale, very fair, ruddy freckled; thin sensitive dry skin, burns easily, ages rapidly; skin cancer most common; avoid sun and harsh treatments.

nodes.label: EP Class II (Caucasian II)
nodes.summary: Central/Southern European and USA origin; fair with light olive undertones; burns then tans, early aging, acne prone, greater skin cancer risk; peels and lasers with caution.

nodes.label: EP Class III (Caucasian III)
nodes.summary: Australia, Turkey, South Africa etc.; fair medium olive; seldom burns, normal to oily skin; thicker darker scars; hyperpigmentation tendency with sun.

nodes.label: EP Class IV (Hispanic/Latino)
nodes.summary: Latin American origin; medium to dark olive; rarely burns, moderate aging, darker scars; hyperpigmentation, acne prone; caution with deep peels and laser.

nodes.label: EP Class V (Mediterranean/Asian I)
nodes.summary: Middle East and Central Asia origin; medium-dark olive; seldom burns; hyperpigmentation/melasma, PIH with acne; skin cancer rare; caution with deeper peels and laser.

nodes.label: EP Class VI (Asian II)
nodes.summary: East and Southeast Asian origin; medium-dark yellow-olive; ages well; prone to hyperpigmentation, melasma and PIH; may react to retinoids and hydroquinone.

nodes.label: EP Class VII (Asian III)
nodes.summary: South Asian origin (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh); light to dark olive with yellow undertones; rarely burns; hyperpigmentation, melasma, acne, PIH; sensitive to retinoids and hydroquinone; keloid tendency.

nodes.label: EP Class VIII (Pacific Islander)
nodes.summary: Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander origin; medium-dark olive, thick oily skin; prone to hyperpigmentation, melasma; keloid tendency.

nodes.label: EP Class IX (Native American/Alaskan)
nodes.summary: Native American and Alaskan origin; medium olive with red undertones; high sun tolerance, leathery with age; hyperpigmentation/melasma.

nodes.label: EP Class X (Black/African American)
nodes.summary: African and Caribbean origin; medium-dark brown; never burns; pigmentation issues, keloids, pseudofolliculitis; skin cancer very rare; extreme caution with peels and lasers.

nodes.label: EP Class XI (Mixed Race)
nodes.summary: Mix of two or more races; consider predominant traits, start with milder programs and evaluate ancestry before peels, lasers, hydroquinone or retinoids.

nodes.label: Skin of Color
nodes.summary: Skin with enough pigment to impart a color other than white (African, Asian, Latin, Native American, Pacific Islander, mixed origin); global skin color landscape shifting toward darker tones.

nodes.label: Hyperpigmentation
nodes.summary: Excess melanin causing dark spots; common precaution for olive and darker EP classes, especially with excessive sun exposure.

nodes.label: Melasma
nodes.summary: Acquired patchy facial hyperpigmentation common in EP classes V-X.

nodes.label: Post-Inflammatory Hyperpigmentation
nodes.summary: Pigment increase after inflammation such as acne; prominent in Asian, Mediterranean and African skin classes.

nodes.label: Keloid
nodes.summary: Large raised abnormal scar; tendency noted in Asian III, Pacific Islander and Black skin classes.

nodes.label: Pseudofolliculitis Barbae
nodes.summary: Razor bumps from ingrown curled hairs; listed for Black/African American skin class.

nodes.label: Hydroquinone
nodes.summary: Skin-lightening agent; Asian and mixed skin classes may react to it, requiring caution.

nodes.label: Retinoids
nodes.summary: Vitamin A derivatives; Asian skin classes may react or be sensitive to retinoids.

nodes.label: Chemical Peel
nodes.summary: Exfoliating treatment of varying depth; deep peels require caution in darker skin classes due to hyperpigmentation and keloid risk.

nodes.label: Laser Treatment
nodes.summary: Facial laser procedures requiring caution in olive and dark skin classes due to hyperpigmentation and keloid risk.

nodes.label: Wood's Lamp Examination
nodes.summary: UV lamp examination used to check for photodamage, congested skin and hyperpigmentation/melasma and pigment depth.

nodes.label: UV Photography
nodes.summary: UV photo through a Canfield polarized camera documenting UV photodamage.

nodes.label: Skin Evaluation Questionnaire
nodes.summary: Three-page intake form covering skin type, ancestry, tanning, pigmentation, vascularity, acne, sun exposure, free radical exposure, lifestyle and healing ability.

nodes.label: Skin Type (Oily/Dry)
nodes.summary: Categorization from very dry to very oily and blemished, based on T-zone and cheek oiliness.

nodes.label: Skin Undertone
nodes.summary: Complexion undertones vary by region: yellow/olive in Asia, ruddy red/pink in Europe; lighter in northern climates, darker near the equator.

nodes.label: Sun Exposure
nodes.summary: Exposure to sunlight; most damage accumulated during the first 18 years of life; key driver of photodamage and pigmentation.

nodes.label: United States
nodes.summary: Diverse country: 2010 census 308.7 million, 63.7% White non-Hispanic single race, 16.3% Hispanic, 12.2% Black, 4.7% Asian.

nodes.label: Dermatologic Disorders in Skin of Color
nodes.summary: Reviews disorders more common or more noticeable in skin of color, framed by Fitzpatrick phototypes: melasma, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, vitiligo, idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis and pseudofolliculitis barbae, with their causes and treatments (hydroquinone, natural lighteners, phototherapy, etc.).

nodes.label: Vitiligo
nodes.summary: Acquired depigmentation affecting 0.5-1% of the population, with absence of melanocytes; likely autoimmune in genetically predisposed people; localized, generalized or universal (>=80% involvement).

nodes.label: Idiopathic Guttate Hypomelanosis
nodes.summary: Hypopigmented 1-6 mm spots on forearms and shins affecting nearly 80% of people over 70; sun exposure thought to play a role.

nodes.label: Tretinoin
nodes.summary: All-trans retinoic acid; added to hydroquinone to enhance efficacy against hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Kojic Acid
nodes.summary: Non-FDA-approved natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation; used in combination peels for melasma.

nodes.label: Arbutin
nodes.summary: Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Soy
nodes.summary: Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Licorice Extract
nodes.summary: Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Rucinol
nodes.summary: Non-FDA-approved alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Mulberry Extract
nodes.summary: Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Niacinamide
nodes.summary: Vitamin B3 amide; listed as alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Ellagic Acid
nodes.summary: Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Resveratrol
nodes.summary: Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Dioic Acid
nodes.summary: Alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.

nodes.label: Narrow-Band UVB Phototherapy
nodes.summary: Gold standard and most frequently used treatment for vitiligo.

nodes.label: Excimer Laser
nodes.summary: Laser option for vitiligo treatment.

nodes.label: Topical Corticosteroids
nodes.summary: Steroids used for vitiligo and, at low potency, for pseudofolliculitis inflammation.

nodes.label: Topical Calcineurin Inhibitors
nodes.summary: Treatment option for vitiligo.

nodes.label: Vitamin D3 Analogs
nodes.summary: Topical treatment option for vitiligo.

nodes.label: Monobenzone
nodes.summary: Agent for total depigmentation reserved as last resort in extensive recalcitrant vitiligo.

nodes.label: Cosmetic Camouflage
nodes.summary: Cover makeup helpful to conceal vitiligo on face and neck.

nodes.label: Cryotherapy
nodes.summary: Liquid nitrogen treatment for idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis; risks post-inflammatory hyper/hypopigmentation in dark skin.

nodes.label: Eflornithine
nodes.summary: Cream option for treating pseudofolliculitis barbae.

nodes.label: Laser Hair Removal
nodes.summary: Treatment option for pseudofolliculitis barbae.

nodes.label: Chemical Depilatory
nodes.summary: Hair removal option for pseudofolliculitis barbae.

nodes.label: Autoimmunity
nodes.summary: Immune attack on self; strongest evidence for vitiligo pathogenesis; vitiligo associated with other autoimmune diseases.

nodes.label: Koebnerization
nodes.summary: Propensity of lesions such as vitiligo to occur at sites of trauma.

nodes.label: Food and Drug Administration
nodes.summary: US agency; approved hydroquinone 4% for hyperpigmentation and tretinoin for wrinkles.

nodes.label: Specialty Corrective Cosmeceuticals for Asian Ethnic Skin
nodes.summary: Defines the Asian ethnic skin market (EP classes V-VII) and the cultural demand for fair skin driving a large skin-lightening market in India, China and Japan. Explains melanin differences (pheomelanin yellow undertones), common pigmentary and other conditions of ethnic skin, preventive regimens and treatments (exfoliation, peels, microdermabrasion, IPL, sunscreen).

nodes.label: Asian Ethnic Skin
nodes.summary: Skin of EP classes V-VII with yellow undertones from higher pheomelanin; prone to pigmentation disorders and acne in normal to oily skin; aging shows as hyperpigmentation rather than wrinkles.

nodes.label: Skin Lightening Product
nodes.summary: Whitening/brightening creams; about 60% of Indian women use daily; 71% of China's skin care market; Asia-Pacific market projected over $2 billion by 2012.

nodes.label: India
nodes.summary: Cosmetics industry expected to reach US$3.6 billion by 2014; skin-lightening cream market US$432 million in 2010 growing 18% annually; fair skin rooted in culture and caste.

nodes.label: China
nodes.summary: Skin care market over 35 billion yuan (US$5.5 billion), of which whitening products are 71%.

nodes.label: Japan
nodes.summary: Dominates global skin lighteners market; cosmetics industry reported growing at 17% a year.

nodes.label: Periorbital Hypermelanosis
nodes.summary: Under-eye dark circles, very common in Asian (especially Indian) populations; hereditary or from stress, eye strain, allergies, smoking, alcohol, caffeine, poor sleep and diet.

nodes.label: Photomelanosis
nodes.summary: Increased pigmentation on sun-exposed skin (face, neck, back), patchy or diffuse; also called sun damage.

nodes.label: Seborrheic Dermatitis
nodes.summary: Dandruff-type condition common in brown skin, involving hairline, scalp, eyebrows, nasolabial folds and ears.

nodes.label: Hypopigmentation
nodes.summary: Loss of pigment when melanocytes no longer function; from overbleaching or trauma from UV, lasers or heat; includes vitiligo and albinism.

nodes.label: Albinism
nodes.summary: Rare inherited absence of a melanin-producing enzyme causing complete lack of pigmentation; high sun damage and skin cancer risk.

nodes.label: Microdermabrasion
nodes.summary: Vacuum suction with diamond chips or aluminum oxide crystals exfoliating top skin layers; improves melasma over multiple treatments.

nodes.label: Trichloroacetic Acid Peel
nodes.summary: TCA peel, safe with experienced dermatologists, good option for severe melasma.

nodes.label: Glycolic Acid
nodes.summary: Alpha hydroxy acid; 30-70% glycolic acid peels common for melasma; increases SC turnover.

nodes.label: Lactic Acid
nodes.summary: Alpha hydroxy acid used in combination and lactic peels; long-known moisturizer.

nodes.label: Alpha Hydroxy Acids
nodes.summary: Hydroxy acids such as glycolic and lactic acid used in peels and anti-aging products.

nodes.label: Intense Pulsed Light
nodes.summary: IPL with pigmentation filter reduces pigmentation, usually 3-4 treatments at 15-20 day intervals.

nodes.label: Fractional Laser
nodes.summary: Fractional laser treatments used to reduce pigmentation.

nodes.label: Exfoliation
nodes.summary: Mechanical or chemical removal of dead skin cells three times weekly to increase cellular turnover and speed brightening results.

nodes.label: Cosmeceutical
nodes.summary: Cosmetic products with active, skin-altering effects; corrective cosmeceuticals for ethnic skin must address multiple conditions.

nodes.label: Compromised Skin in the Elderly
nodes.summary: Reviews skin structure and the effects of intrinsic and extrinsic (photo) aging on the stratum corneum, epidermis and dermis, including barrier function, TEWL, dry skin, mechanical properties, telangiectasia and photo-aging mechanisms. Covers treatments: sunscreens, tretinoin and cosmeceuticals (retinol, niacinamide, hydroxy acids, antioxidants, peptides).

nodes.label: Intrinsic Aging
nodes.summary: Unavoidable effect of time on all body sites, independent of lifestyle; reduces collagen synthesis, flattens the dermal-epidermal junction; both collagen and elastin decrease.

nodes.label: Extrinsic Aging
nodes.summary: Aging from lifestyle choices, mainly UV photo-aging and also cigarette smoke exposure.

nodes.label: Cigarette Smoking
nodes.summary: Cigarette smoke exposure causes significant skin compromise in smokers and nonsmoking spouses; associated with telangiectasia and premature wrinkling.

nodes.label: Type I Collagen
nodes.summary: Predominant collagen of the reticular dermis; reduced in photo-aged skin.

nodes.label: Type III Collagen
nodes.summary: Collagen of the papillary dermis, low in reticular dermis; reduced in photo-aged skin.

nodes.label: Procollagen
nodes.summary: Precursor synthesized in fibroblasts and processed by proteolytic enzymes into 300-nm collagen triple helix filaments.

nodes.label: Oxytalan Fiber
nodes.summary: Thin (10-12 nm) elastic fibers perpendicular to the DEJ in papillary dermis; shortened and nearly gone by the ninth decade.

nodes.label: Elaunin Fiber
nodes.summary: Elastic fibers parallel to the skin plane in papillary dermis; network gradually lost with age.

nodes.label: Desmosine
nodes.summary: Cross-link binding four elastin chains, formed from three allysine and one lysine.

nodes.label: Lysyl Oxidase
nodes.summary: Enzyme converting lysine to allysine in elastin.

nodes.label: Proteoglycan
nodes.summary: GAGs such as chondroitin and keratan sulfate bound to core proteins; link proteins bind them to HA forming a hygroscopic complex.

nodes.label: Histamine
nodes.summary: Released from mast cell granules in response to heat or irritants.

nodes.label: Peptidylarginine Deiminase
nodes.summary: Enzyme converting filaggrin arginine to citrulline, releasing it from microfibrils.

nodes.label: Pyrrolidone Carboxylic Acid
nodes.summary: Very hydrophilic NMF component formed from glutamine; lower in elderly skin, especially deeper in the SC.

nodes.label: Glycerol
nodes.summary: Derived from sebum hydrolysis; contributes to skin hydration (asebic mice studies).

nodes.label: Dry Skin
nodes.summary: Xerosis common in the elderly, prone to itching, with distinctive line patterns on legs; multifactorial (lower PCA, slower SC renewal, less lactate and glycerol).

nodes.label: Pruritus
nodes.summary: Itching, especially common and sometimes severe in elderly dry skin.

nodes.label: Skin Irritation
nodes.summary: Reactivity to irritants (SLS, soap, octanoic acid); decreases or is not more marked with age.

nodes.label: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
nodes.summary: Surfactant irritant; older skin shows lower reactivity to SLS.

nodes.label: Barrier Recovery
nodes.summary: Repair of SC barrier after tape stripping or acetone; young skin recovers 50% in 24 h vs 15% in over-80s; 90% recovery takes 4 vs 7 days.

nodes.label: Stratum Corneum Turnover
nodes.summary: SC renewal time, measured by dansyl chloride, increases from 19.8 days (under 35) to 28.1 days (over 60) due to decreased epidermal proliferation.

nodes.label: Dansyl Chloride Turnover Assay
nodes.summary: Staining SC with fluorescent dansyl chloride and monitoring disappearance under UV light to measure SC turnover time.

nodes.label: Dermatoglyphic Pattern
nodes.summary: Pattern of shallow surface lines in young skin that becomes fewer, deeper and more oriented with aging.

nodes.label: Langer's Lines
nodes.summary: Natural lines of tension in the skin that may influence orientation of aging line patterns.

nodes.label: Cutometer
nodes.summary: Most common skin elasticity instrument using negative pressure (20-500 mbar) suction probes; parameters Ue, Uv, Uf, Ur, Ua, R and ratios like Ur/Uf.

nodes.label: Skin Elasticity
nodes.summary: Viscoelastic property; extensibility (Uf) and elastic recovery (Ur/Uf) decrease with age, Ur/Uf most strongly (R2=0.656).

nodes.label: Skin Sagging
nodes.summary: Sagging correlated with decreased Ur/Uf on the cheeks.

nodes.label: Telangiectasia
nodes.summary: Visible surface blood vessels developing with age from dermal thinning or chronic sun exposure; associated with smoking.

nodes.label: Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor
nodes.summary: Angiogenic factor up-regulated by UVB in keratinocytes, endothelial cells and fibroblasts.

nodes.label: Thrombospondin-1
nodes.summary: Endogenous inhibitor of blood-vessel growth down-regulated by UVB.

nodes.label: Nucleotide Excision Repair
nodes.summary: DNA repair system whose capacity declines with age.

nodes.label: Telomere Shortening
nodes.summary: Telomeres are especially sensitive to UV damage; shortening may significantly affect photo-aging.

nodes.label: MAP Kinase Pathway
nodes.summary: Mitogen-activated protein kinase cascade activated by ROS-induced cytokines leading to AP-1 formation.

nodes.label: AP-1
nodes.summary: Transcription factor promoting MMP/collagenase transcription and reducing fibroblast sensitivity to TGF-beta.

nodes.label: Transforming Growth Factor Beta
nodes.summary: Growth factor stimulating collagen production; fibroblast sensitivity reduced by AP-1.

nodes.label: Solar Elastosis
nodes.summary: Hallmark of photo-aging: accumulation of dystrophic elastic fibers with lysozyme and amyloid P that provide little elasticity.

nodes.label: Wrinkles
nodes.summary: Visible sign of aging; crow's feet number peaks about age 35 while depth increases eightfold from 35 to 65.

nodes.label: Beta-Carotene
nodes.summary: Oral supplementation in Nambour trial showed no difference from placebo on photo-aging.

nodes.label: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
nodes.summary: US law that does not recognize cosmeceuticals; a product is a drug, a cosmetic or both.

nodes.label: Retinol
nodes.summary: Vitamin A; produces tretinoin-like changes, much less effective but less irritating; 0.15% improves wrinkling and hyperpigmentation in 12 weeks; can be unstable.

nodes.label: Retinyl Propionate
nodes.summary: Retinol ester; 0.3% improved wrinkling and hyperpigmentation after 12 weeks.

nodes.label: Retinyl Palmitate
nodes.summary: Retinol ester shown to be metabolized to retinol and free acid in skin.

nodes.label: Salicylic Acid
nodes.summary: Basis of beta hydroxy acid products, usually about 2%.

nodes.label: Beta Hydroxy Acids
nodes.summary: So-called BHA products based on salicylic acid.

nodes.label: Tocopherol
nodes.summary: Vitamin E, among the most studied antioxidants for photo-aging protection.

nodes.label: Green Tea Polyphenols
nodes.summary: Most studied plant antioxidants; promising in mice but human trials failed to show visible anti-aging benefit, though elastic tissue improved histologically.

nodes.label: Peptides
nodes.summary: Investigated actives for improving compromised elderly skin.

nodes.label: Anti-Glycation Compounds
nodes.summary: Compounds investigated for improving aged skin.

nodes.label: Skin Aging
nodes.summary: Age-related skin changes divided into intrinsic and extrinsic aging; wrinkles and color inhomogeneity drive apparent age.
